prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a side impact at intersection in Katy, Texas, and has whiplash. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1241; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This call is being recorded for claim documentation. Can you please state your full name for the record?

A: I'd rather just give my first name for now, if that's okay. Everything else is in the paperwork I sent.

Q: That works. Can you walk me through what happened at the intersection?

A: I was going through a green light heading east, and a car coming from the north side turned left in front of me. I tried to brake, but there wasn't enough time. They hit my driver's side door.

Q: Did the other driver say anything at the scene?

A: They said they didn't see me. They seemed pretty shaken up, honestly.

Q: How fast would you estimate you were traveling when the impact occurred?

A: Probably around the speed limit, maybe a little under. I wasn't speeding.

Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt?

A: Yes, I was.

Q: Did you go to the hospital or see a doctor after the collision?

A: The paramedics checked me out at the scene, and then I went to an urgent care clinic later that afternoon. They diagnosed whiplash and told me to rest my neck.

Q: Are you currently receiving any treatment?

A: I've been going to physical therapy twice a week. My neck is still stiff, and I get headaches when I'm at the computer for long periods.

Q: Have you missed any time from work because of your injuries?

A: A few days right after the accident. I'm back now, but I'm on lighter duties for a while.

Q: Is there anything else you think I should know about the accident or your injuries?

A: No, I think that covers it. Let me know if you need any of my medical records.

Q: Thank you. We'll follow up with you once the review is complete.
